punchline: When the first honest feedback someone gets is the day they're fired, the kindness came far too late to help.
thirty_sec: Early in her career, Kim Scott managed Bob, a charming, well-liked employee whose work kept falling short. Not wanting to hurt him, she softened or skipped her criticism and kept encouraging him. His teammates redid his work and began doubting her. After about ten months she had to fire him, and he asked why nobody had told him. Scott calls this 'ruinous empathy': caring personally without challenging directly.
question: If your work were falling short, would you want to hear it in the first month or the tenth?
